title: ML-EAT: A Multilevel Embedding Association Test for Interpretable and Transparent Social Science

bias_targets.methodology: Applying the Multilevel Embedding Association Test (ML-EAT) to measure differential cosine similarities between male/female concepts and attributes like career/family, math/arts, and science/arts using static word, language, and image embeddings.
Using ML-EAT to evaluate differential cosine similarities between European American/African American names or White/Black images and pleasant/unpleasant attributes.
Using ML-EAT to evaluate associations between young/old concepts (names and images) and pleasant/unpleasant attributes based on underlying cosine similarity distributions.
Measuring differential cosine similarities between thin/heavy image concepts and pleasant/unpleasant textual attributes using ML-EAT on multimodal CLIP embeddings.

Evaluating cosine similarity associations between religious identities (Christianity/Judaism, Arab-Muslim/Non-Arab-Muslim) and pleasant/unpleasant attributes using ML-EAT in language-and-image models.
Computing ML-EAT effect sizes and underlying cosine similarities between abled/disabled concepts and pleasant/unpleasant attributes in multimodal embeddings.
Applying ML-EAT to measure differential cosine similarity associations between straight/gay concepts and pleasant/unpleasant attributes.
Measuring differential associations between light-skin/dark-skin concepts and pleasant/unpleasant attributes using the ML-EAT framework on CLIP models.

Applying ML-EAT to standard psychological IAT baselines (e.g., Flowers/Insects, Instruments/Weapons, Mental/Physical disease) to quantify associations with pleasant/unpleasant or temporary/permanent attributes.
